History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
30-y-o female nurse with 7-day history of persistent fever, alternating chills/sweats, myalgia, nausea, and fatigue after recent rural travel to Vietnam; needs urgent in-person assessment and blood tests to rule out malaria and other infectious causes.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Fever with drenching sweats for 7 days.  
• Timeline: Began ~1 week ago; persistent despite OTC paracetamol/ibuprofen (only partial, temporary relief). Returned from Vietnam 4 weeks ago.  
• Character: Episodes of feeling very hot and sweaty alternating with feeling cold; night sweats present.  
• Associated symptoms: Generalized muscle aches, nausea with ↓ appetite, mild fluid intake, marked tiredness.  
• Pertinent negatives: No cough, sore throat, ear pain, diarrhea, urinary frequency/dysuria, neck stiffness, new-onset headache, rash, or joint swelling.  
• Screen-related chronic headaches unchanged.  
• No clear localizing source of infection identified during ROS.

Past Medical History:
• Chronic mechanical back pain related to prolonged sitting/poor posture – under active physiotherapy.  
• Episodic tension/migraine headaches triggered by screen use/weather.  
• No other significant illnesses reported.

Medications:
• Seroxat (paroxetine) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Paracetamol – OTC, dose/route/frequency not documented (symptomatic).  
• Ibuprofen – OTC, dose/route/frequency not documented (symptomatic).  
• Recent malaria prophylaxis (daily regimen, unspecified drug) during Vietnam trip – completed; exact details unknown.

Allergies:
• Pollen (hay fever). No drug allergies reported.

Social History:
• Occupation: Nurse; currently struggling to work due to fatigue.  
• Tobacco: Non-smoker.  
• Alcohol: Moderate intake.  
• Exercise: Moderate several times per week.  
• Vaccinations: Up-to-date including Hepatitis B.  
• Recent travel: 3-week trip to Vietnam (cities, rural trekking/cycling, river/farmland exposure); returned 4 weeks ago.

Family History:
• Father died of myocardial infarction at age 68.  
• No other familial illnesses mentioned.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (telephone consult).  
• Examination findings: Not recorded (patient not yet seen).

Investigations:
• Planned: Thick & thin blood films for malaria; inflammatory markers; additional baseline bloods (FBC, U&E, LFT, CRP/ESR) and other tests per clinician’s discretion after physical exam.  
• No results yet.

Assessment & Plan:
Overall Impression:
Undifferentiated febrile illness one week in duration after recent travel to malaria-endemic area; malaria must be excluded; alternative viral or other tropical infections also considered.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Malaria – High suspicion: travel to rural Vietnam, fever with chills/sweats; prophylaxis not fully protective.  
2. Acute systemic viral infection (e.g., influenza/COVID-19) – Possible: constitutional symptoms without focus, but persistent high fever beyond typical course.  
3. Dengue/other arboviral infection – Consider: endemic region exposure; less likely given late onset and absent rash/arthralgia.

Issue 1 – Febrile illness of unknown origin post-travel:  
• Plan:  
  – Urgent in-person evaluation at central London clinic (or local A&E if unable).  
  – Full physical examination and vitals.  
  – Labs: Thick/thin blood films for malaria; malaria rapid antigen if available; FBC, U&E, LFT, CRP/ESR, blood cultures; consider dengue/typhoid serology based on findings.  
  – Advise patient not to work until cause identified.  
  – Safety-net: Seek emergency care if deteriorating, altered consciousness, rigors, jaundice, or bleeding.  
  – Follow-up: Clinic to contact with results; telephone review within 24–48 h or sooner if malaria positive.

Issue 2 – Chronic mechanical back pain:  
• Stable; continue physiotherapy exercises; no change in management today.

Issue 3 – Ongoing psychotropic therapy (Seroxat):  
• Continue current regimen; monitor mood; no adjustments planned today.

General plan items:  
• Administrative: Doctor to send message to admin team; patient to phone provided number to schedule same-day appointment.  
• Documentation: Summary of clinical reasoning and required tests to be included in referral note for receiving clinician.

Quality checks:
• Missing vitals and physical exam – to be obtained at clinic visit.  
• Medication doses/routes/frequencies not documented.  
• Exact malaria prophylaxis agent unknown.  
• No documented drug allergies (only pollen); confirm at face-to-face visit.  
• Transcript quality: Clear; minor conversational fillers removed; no conflicting statements noted between transcript and DDx.
